title: Basic Nursing Care — Documentation, SBAR Reporting & Delegation Basics (Set 15)
subtitle: Purposes and qualities of good documentation, timing and integrity of chart entries, the SBAR communication format, safe shift handoff, the delegation process and the 'rights' of delegation, accepting/clarifying delegated tasks within scope, and reporting back
scenario: Communicating and documenting safely: recording care accurately and on time, using SBAR to report clearly, handing off at shift change, and working within delegation and scope while reporting results back to the nurse.

steps.q: A primary purpose of documentation in the client's record is to:

opts.text: Communicate care to the team, provide a legal record, and support continuity of care
opts.rat: The record shares information among caregivers, serves as a legal document, and lets care continue safely across shifts.

opts.text: Serve only as optional busywork
opts.rat: Documentation is essential to communication, safety, and the legal record, not busywork.

opts.text: Provide entertainment for staff
opts.rat: Documentation has clinical and legal purposes, not entertainment.

opts.text: Replace all verbal communication permanently
opts.rat: Documentation complements—rather than replaces—necessary verbal communication such as reports and handoffs.

steps.q: Good documentation should be:

opts.text: Accurate, factual, objective, timely, legible, and complete
opts.rat: These qualities make the record trustworthy and useful for safe, continuous care.

opts.text: Vague, delayed, and based on opinion
opts.rat: Vague, delayed, opinion-based notes undermine safety and accuracy.

opts.text: Written illegibly to save time
opts.rat: Illegible entries can cause errors; documentation must be legible.

opts.text: Exaggerated to make a point
opts.rat: Exaggeration falsifies the record; documentation is factual.

steps.q: When should care be documented?

opts.text: Promptly after the care is provided—never charted in advance
opts.rat: Charting soon after care keeps the record accurate; documenting care before it is done is falsification and dangerous.

opts.text: Before the care is actually given, to save time
opts.rat: Charting ahead is falsification; care is documented after it is performed.

opts.text: Several days later from memory
opts.rat: Delayed charting is inaccurate; documentation should be timely.

opts.text: Only at the end of the month
opts.rat: Care is documented promptly, not batched far later.

steps.q: To maintain the integrity of a paper chart, the technician should:

opts.text: Avoid leaving blank lines or gaps that others could fill in later
opts.rat: Blank spaces can be altered or added to; keeping entries continuous protects the record's integrity.

opts.text: Leave large blank areas between entries
opts.rat: Gaps invite tampering and are avoided.

opts.text: Use white-out to remove mistakes
opts.rat: Correction fluid is never used; errors are corrected per policy (for example, a single line through).

opts.text: Write entries for other staff members
opts.rat: Each caregiver documents their own care, not others'.

steps.q: The SBAR communication format stands for:

opts.text: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
opts.rat: SBAR is a structured way to organize a report: Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation.

opts.text: Start, Begin, Act, Rest
opts.rat: This is not what SBAR stands for.

opts.text: Safety, Billing, Admission, Records
opts.rat: These are not the SBAR components.

opts.text: Sign, Behave, Ask, Report
opts.rat: This is not the SBAR format.

steps.q: In SBAR, the 'Situation' is:

opts.text: A brief statement of the current problem or reason for the report
opts.rat: The Situation concisely states what is happening right now that prompted the communication.

opts.text: The client's entire life history
opts.rat: Detailed history belongs to Background; Situation is the current problem.

opts.text: The recommendation for what to do
opts.rat: That is the Recommendation, not the Situation.

opts.text: The client's insurance details
opts.rat: Administrative details are not the Situation.

steps.q: In SBAR, the 'Background' provides:

opts.text: Relevant history and context related to the current situation
opts.rat: Background gives the pertinent history and context needed to understand the situation.

opts.text: The final decision about treatment
opts.rat: Decisions/requests are the Recommendation, not Background.

opts.text: Only the client's favorite foods
opts.rat: Preferences unrelated to the issue are not relevant background.

opts.text: The technician's personal opinions about coworkers
opts.rat: Personal opinions are not part of a professional SBAR report.

steps.q: In SBAR, the 'Assessment' (within the technician's scope) includes:

opts.text: The technician's relevant observations and what they think the concern is
opts.rat: The Assessment shares pertinent observations and the reporter's read of the situation, within their scope.

opts.text: A formal medical diagnosis
opts.rat: Diagnosing is outside the technician's scope; they report observations and concerns.

opts.text: Nothing at all
opts.rat: The Assessment does convey observations and the reason for concern.

opts.text: The billing code for the visit
opts.rat: Billing is not part of the SBAR assessment.

steps.q: In SBAR, the 'Recommendation' is:

opts.text: What the reporter is requesting or suggesting be done next
opts.rat: The Recommendation states what the reporter needs—for example, asking the nurse to assess the client or give direction.

opts.text: A restatement of the client's birthdate
opts.rat: That is not the Recommendation.

opts.text: The client's meal order
opts.rat: A meal order is not the SBAR recommendation.

opts.text: The weather report
opts.rat: This is irrelevant to SBAR.

steps.q: The main benefit of using SBAR is that it:

opts.text: Organizes communication so it is clear and complete, helping reduce errors
opts.rat: A structured format ensures important information is conveyed clearly and completely, improving safety.

opts.text: Makes reports longer and more confusing
opts.rat: SBAR streamlines and clarifies communication.

opts.text: Lets staff leave out important information
opts.rat: SBAR is designed to include the key information, not omit it.

opts.text: Replaces the need to document
opts.rat: SBAR structures verbal reporting; documentation is still required.

steps.q: A good shift handoff (end-of-shift report) provides:

opts.text: Organized, accurate, relevant information so the next caregiver can safely continue care
opts.rat: A clear, accurate handoff of the pertinent information supports safe continuity of care between shifts.

opts.text: Only gossip about the clients
opts.rat: Handoff is professional and clinical, not gossip.

opts.text: As little information as possible
opts.rat: Withholding relevant information endangers continuity and safety.

opts.text: Made-up details to fill time
opts.rat: Handoff must be accurate; fabrication is unsafe.

steps.q: When the technician needs to report a change in a client's condition to the nurse, the communication should be:

opts.text: Prompt, clear, and organized (for example, using SBAR)
opts.rat: Timely, well-organized reporting—such as SBAR—helps the nurse understand and act on the concern quickly.

opts.text: Delayed and disorganized
opts.rat: Delay and disorganization can lead to missed or mishandled problems.

opts.text: Left as a vague hint
opts.rat: Vague reporting risks the concern being missed.

opts.text: Skipped entirely if the technician is busy
opts.rat: Changes in condition are always reported, regardless of workload.

steps.q: Delegation in nursing refers to:

opts.text: A licensed nurse assigning a task to the technician to perform within the technician's training and scope
opts.rat: The nurse delegates appropriate tasks that the technician is trained and permitted to perform.

opts.text: The technician assigning tasks to the nurse
opts.rat: Delegation flows from the licensed nurse to the technician, not the reverse.

opts.text: Clients deciding staff assignments
opts.rat: Delegation is a professional nursing responsibility, not decided by clients.

opts.text: Performing any task regardless of training
opts.rat: Delegated tasks must be within the technician's training and scope.

steps.q: The commonly taught 'rights of delegation' include the right:

opts.text: Task, circumstances, person, direction/communication, and supervision
opts.rat: These 'five rights' guide safe delegation: the right task, under the right circumstances, to the right person, with clear direction and appropriate supervision.

opts.text: Color, size, weight, and shape
opts.rat: These are not the rights of delegation.

opts.text: Speed, secrecy, and shortcuts
opts.rat: These are unsafe and are not delegation principles.

opts.text: Cost, brand, and packaging
opts.rat: These are unrelated to delegation.

steps.q: Before accepting a delegated task, the technician should ensure that it:

opts.text: Is within their training, scope, and competence—and clarify with the nurse if unsure
opts.rat: Accepting only tasks one is trained and permitted to do, and clarifying uncertainty, keeps clients safe.

opts.text: Is accepted without any thought
opts.rat: The technician confirms the task is appropriate before accepting.

opts.text: Is performed even if clearly beyond scope
opts.rat: Tasks outside scope are not performed; the technician clarifies or declines.

opts.text: Is done secretly without reporting results
opts.rat: Results are reported back; secrecy is not appropriate.

steps.q: If a nurse delegates a task that is unsafe or outside the technician's scope, the technician should:

opts.text: Respectfully clarify or decline and inform the nurse, rather than performing it
opts.rat: The technician does not perform tasks beyond scope or that are unsafe; clarifying or declining and communicating protects the client.

opts.text: Perform it anyway to avoid conflict
opts.rat: Performing an unsafe or out-of-scope task endangers the client and the technician.

opts.text: Do it and hide any problems
opts.rat: Concealing problems is unsafe and improper.

opts.text: Delegate it to a client
opts.rat: Tasks are not delegated to clients.

steps.q: After completing a delegated task, the technician should:

opts.text: Report the outcome and any relevant observations back to the delegating nurse and document as required
opts.rat: Reporting results and observations back closes the loop, lets the nurse follow up, and keeps the record accurate.

opts.text: Say nothing, since the task is finished
opts.rat: The nurse needs the results to continue safe care; report back.

opts.text: Only report if something went wrong
opts.rat: Outcomes are reported whether or not a problem occurred.

opts.text: Report to a different client instead
opts.rat: Results go to the delegating nurse, not to another client.

steps.q: Which type of responsibility generally CANNOT be delegated to the technician?

opts.text: Professional nursing judgment such as client assessment, evaluation, and teaching
opts.rat: Higher-level nursing judgment—assessment, evaluation, and teaching—remains with the licensed nurse and is not delegated to the technician.

opts.text: A routine task within the technician's training
opts.rat: Routine tasks within training are appropriately delegated.

opts.text: Assisting a client with hygiene as trained
opts.rat: This is an appropriate delegated task within scope.

opts.text: Reporting observations to the nurse
opts.rat: Reporting observations is part of the technician's role, not something that cannot be delegated.

steps.q: When giving or receiving a verbal report, information about the client should be shared:

opts.text: Only with those involved in the client's care and in a private, professional manner
opts.rat: Client information is shared on a need-to-know basis and kept confidential, consistent with privacy requirements.

opts.text: Loudly in a public hallway
opts.rat: Discussing client information where others can overhear breaches confidentiality.

opts.text: With anyone who is curious
opts.rat: Information is limited to those involved in care, not the merely curious.

opts.text: On social media for efficiency
opts.rat: Sharing client information on social media violates confidentiality.

steps.q: Overall, effective communication and delegation practice for the technician means:

opts.text: Documenting accurately and on time, reporting clearly (e.g., SBAR) and handing off safely, and working within delegation/scope while reporting results back
opts.rat: Accurate documentation, structured reporting and handoff, and working within scope with report-back together support safe, coordinated care.

opts.text: Charting in advance and reporting vaguely
opts.rat: Advance charting and vague reports are unsafe and improper.

opts.text: Performing any delegated task regardless of scope and never reporting back
opts.rat: Tasks must be within scope, and results are reported back.

opts.text: Keeping information from the care team
opts.rat: Relevant information is communicated to the team for safe care.

reference: Aligned to the California BVNPT Psychiatric Technician exam content area: Basic Nursing Care (documentation, reporting, and delegation basics). Written from standard psychiatric-technician and nursing references at an introductory level. Concepts are stated conceptually and marked for faculty confirmation: purposes and qualities of documentation; timely, integrity-preserving charting (documenting after care, avoiding blank gaps, no correction fluid); the SBAR format (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) and its components; safe shift handoff; delegation as a nurse-to-technician process; the 'five rights' of delegation (task, circumstances, person, direction/communication, supervision); accepting only in-scope tasks and clarifying/declining unsafe ones; reporting results back; and that professional nursing judgment (assessment, evaluation, teaching) is not delegated to the technician. Confidentiality in reporting is consistent with privacy requirements. Complements documentation-quality/error-correction items in legal-core-01/02, scope/delegation/accountability items in legal-core-03/04, objective documentation in mh-core-20, and the many 'report to the nurse' items across the BNC sets. No specific numbers, doses, or lab values are asserted. Pending faculty review.
